info.description: Bounded simulator subset of the official AWS Network Firewall API (2020-11-12). Every other official operation returns HTTP 501 UnknownOperationException. Firewall policies, rule groups and TLS inspection configurations are stored configuration records: no firewall, firewall endpoint, VPC endpoint association, proxy or traffic inspection exists, so no packet is ever filtered, decrypted or logged and no rule is evaluated. Firewalls, VPC endpoint associations, proxies, resource policies, logging, analysis reports, flow operations, AWS managed rule groups and every other official operation return UnknownOperationException with HTTP 501, and a policy's NumberOfAssociations is always 0. Every create, describe and update returns an UpdateToken, and the update operations fail with InvalidTokenException and change nothing unless the UpdateToken they carry equals the current one; each successful update issues a new token. An update replaces the whole FirewallPolicy, RuleGroup or TLSInspectionConfiguration body it carries. Deleting a resource removes it at once and the response reports the status DELETING. A firewall policy may reference only rule groups and a TLS inspection configuration of this account that exist, stateless references must name STATELESS groups and stateful references STATEFUL groups, and deleting a rule group or TLS inspection configuration that a policy references fails with InvalidOperationException. Rule group capacity is stored as given and never consumed, so ConsumedCapacity, NumberOfAssociations of rule groups and the consumed capacities of policies are never reported. TLS inspection configurations keep their ACM certificate and certificate authority ARNs without resolving them, so no Certificates or CertificateAuthority status is reported. A rule group takes its rules in RuleGroup; the Rules string is refused, so Suricata rules are given as RuleGroup.RulesSource.RulesString and are stored without being parsed. The rule group ARN carries the lowercased Type (stateful-rulegroup or stateless-rulegroup), names are unique per Region across both types, and a Type sent beside a name or ARN must be the stored one or the group is not found. ListRuleGroups lists the account's own groups: Scope MANAGED and the managed type and subscription filters are refused. DryRun true and AnalyzeRuleGroup true are refused instead of being ignored; false is accepted. A CUSTOMER_KMS EncryptionConfiguration needs a KeyId, which is stored without resolving the key. At most 20 firewall policies, 50 rule groups and 20 TLS inspection configurations exist per Region as local limits, and ListTagsForResource returns every tag in one response and refuses MaxResults and NextToken.
